title: Your best guess against this crowd
hook: Guess 0 to 100: closest to two thirds of the average wins. What wins against this crowd?

knows: the two-thirds game and its ladder to 0 under common knowledge of rationality (two-thirds-of-the-average)
doesNotKnow: that the winning guess depends on what the other players actually guess, so against a crowd that stops after one or two steps, the equilibrium guess 0 loses

misconception: 0 is the rational guess, so it wins.
objective: The learner can explain that the winning guess is two thirds of what the crowd actually averages (their own guess included), so against a crowd that stops after one or two steps the best guess is near 23 and the equilibrium guess 0 loses to most of the crowd.

claims.text: The game's rule, on the stage: 'Target: two thirds of everyone's average.' The target is two thirds of the average of all 101 guesses, the learner's included (predict: 'closest to two thirds of the average, your guess included').
claims.source: The rule of the game as given in brief 3 (Stated model). Demo.tsx avg(g) = (S + g) / 101, target(g) = (2/3)·avg(g), the same formulas as node company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs. Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: Against this crowd the best guess is 2S/301 = 23.01 (S = 3,463), so 23 wins and 0 misses by 22.9 and is beaten by 84 simulated guesses; predict answer B 'About 23' (played: 0 misses by 22.9, 23 by 0.0, 35 by 11.9). Reveal at g = 0: '0 is the equilibrium guess, and it missed by 22.9; 84 simulated guesses were closer.' Every other g: 'Had you guessed 0, the equilibrium, you would have missed by 22.9.'
claims.source: g* solves g = (2/3)(S + g)/101, so g* = 2S/301 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs, checks '(a) best guess', '(a) 0 loses', 'predict answer'; brief 3 claim 2). Demo.tsx computes miss(0) and closer(0) from the seeded crowd. Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: Stage rule line: 'Simulated crowd, seed 2: 30% guess at random, 40% near 33 (one step), 30% near 22 (two steps).' The 100 simulated guesses drawn as dots sum to 3,463 (average 34.6 alone).
claims.source: 100 simulated players, 30 uniform on 0-100, 40 uniform on 30-36, 30 uniform on 19-25, drawn in that order with mulberry32 (src/kit/random.ts, the same generator as the script's) from seed 2; sum 3,463 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs; brief 3 claim 3). Chosen seed, disclosed (pattern disclose-chosen-seeds): the seed is the first from 1 up whose run lies within 0.5 of the rule's expected average 34.8; the comparison draft's seed 7 (average 33.2, on the ladder's 33) and crowd of 99 were replaced (brief 3 seed note, W-1060). 'Near 33' and 'near 22' describe the ranges 30-36 and 19-25. Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: The learner's own screen, conditional on the guess g (0-100): reveal 'With your {g} in, this simulated crowd averaged {avg}, so the target was {target}. Your guess missed by {d}; {k} simulated guesses were closer' ('no simulated guess was closer' at k = 0, only g = 23; '1 simulated guess was closer' at k = 1); stage markers: average (dashed) and target (solid) numerals, the learner's miss bracket and the 0 guess's miss bracket.
claims.source: Computed in Demo.tsx from the seeded crowd and the learner's locked guess with the script's formulas and rounding (one decimal); all 101 guesses print and are checked in node company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs (brief 3 claim 4). Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: Names: 'equilibrium' (predict option A '0, the equilibrium guess'; reveal 'the equilibrium') names the guess that survives the ladder; 'one step' and 'two steps' are the rule's labels for the 40% and 30% groups, linked to two-thirds-of-the-average.
claims.source: Brief 3 claim 5 and Stated model: why the ladder ends at 0 is economics/two-thirds-of-the-average's (published, concept iterated-dominance), linked, not re-derived (E0, E8 (3)). The stage shows no ceiling (66.7, 44.4, ...). Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: HELD (the one type (d) line, every branch, before 'Where it stops'): 'In one online sample of 250 real players, first guesses averaged 36.4, far above 0.'
claims.source: W-902 row 'Beauty contest / level-k' (robust; means vary with population and group size, so a sample is quoted; company/research/notes/2026-10-15-w902-behavioral-economics-replication-sourcing.md): Pantelis & Kennedy 2017, Cognition, PMC5303671 (opened by research-lead, not by the builder or the fact-checker). Fallback (brief 3): cut, nothing replaces it; set HELD_LINE = false in Demo.tsx (reveals 67-74 words). The Nagel 1995 first-round line is not used and stays held (E8 condition 4). Not published until the fact-checker opens it.

claims.text: Reveal, every branch: 'Against a crowd that stops after one or two steps, the winning guess sits near two thirds of the crowd's actual average, not at 0.'
claims.source: Follows from c1-c2: the best reply g* = 2S/(3(N+1) - 2) is close to two thirds of the crowd's average S/N whenever the crowd is large, and is above 0 whenever S > 0; for this crowd 23.01 against 2/3 · 34.63 = 23.09 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs). 'Stops after one or two steps' refers to the rule's labelled groups (c3, c5). Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: Reveal, every branch: 'Where it stops: a simulated crowd with a stated rule, not real players.'
claims.source: About this stage, not about other people (charter rule 5): the crowd is simulated from the rule on the stage (c3). Brief 3 reveal text. Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: Hook: 'Guess 0 to 100: closest to two thirds of the average wins. What wins against this crowd?'
claims.source: States the game's rule (c1) and the slider's range (whole numbers 0-100). Builder's wording (the brief gives no title or hook); it names no answer. Builder statement, not self-verified.

claims.text: Recall answer: a simulated crowd of 100 averages 60 and the target is half the average, your guess included; 'About 30' lands closest (0 misses by 29.7, 30 by 0.1, 60 by 30.0).
claims.source: Target(g) = (6000 + g)/101/2 (node company/domains/briefs/checks/behavioral-beauty-contest-level-k.mjs, recall check; brief 3 transfer recall). Builder statement, not self-verified.

recall.question: A simulated crowd of 100 averages 60. The target is half the average, your guess included. Which guess lands closest?
recall.why: The winning guess sits near the target of what the crowd actually guesses: half of about 60 is about 30. The equilibrium guess 0 misses by about 30.
